terms.grammar: ordinal adjective, first and second declension
evidence: Aur. Vict. Caes. 15.4 (Lewis & Short s.v. nōningentēsimus)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short cites the ordinal only from late writers: nongentēsimus in Aurelius Victor, nōningentēsimus in Priscian. The long ō follows Traupman’s nōngentī; Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
